reviewType: independent, adversarial, live-bytes; derivation RESOLVED not read (freeze 7.3 / CMP-IR-01)
reviewer: independent reviewer, no authorship relationship to versioning-policy.v9 through v14 or to any check-versioning-v*.py
verdictStatement: THE CONTRACT IS CORRECT AND THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT. I resolved the 8-operation derivation independently, with my own resolver, my own type-exact comparator testing bool BEFORE int, and a duplicate-key-rejecting parse, and I reproduced $.resolvedValue.sha256 = 324845b22b3b1aed0dca9deb8fbc032048dc1399da967062c9103332f06aba41 EXACTLY on the first attempt. I re-walked the leaf census from the resolved value and reproduced all ten published categories exactly (1892/119/44/0/103/442/121/0/18, scalarLeaves 2158). The keyLocator is complete and exact as a MAP: 30 entries against 30 resolved top-level keys, no key missing, no key invented, every CHANGED entry naming the correct operation index and pathDisplay and genuinely differing from the predecessor, every INHERITED entry byte-equal to the predecessor and named by no operation. operationAccounting reproduces at 8/6/2, and notInTheOperationList is exactly the 22 untouched predecessor keys - no more, no fewer. THE CENTRAL NEGATIVE CLAIM IS TRUE AND I TESTED IT AS A NEGATIVE. I built a 22-name apparatus vocabulary from the eleven blockers themselves and measured it across the lineage: v9 carries 5 of those keys, v10 9, v11 14, v12 17, v13 20, and versioning-policy.v14.json and its resolved value carry ZERO. I then adjudicated the eleven blockers myself rather than reading the author's reading of them, and every artifact-side leaf any of them names lives under successorRevision.{evidenceEnforcementRepair, enforcementClosureRepair, proseAuthorityRepair, parseAuthorityRepair} or repointRehearsals/residualRestatements/retainedResiduals - blocks v8 does not contain and v14 does not add - while four of the five reviews independently record doesNotAffect: 'status, seal or discharge discipline'. Having no apparatus is a REPAIR here, not an evasion, because the omitted thing is the thing that failed five times and the substantive obligation it replaced - proving a transcription faithful - does not exist when nothing is transcribed. The overstatement scan is CLEAN: zero affirmative claims that V10 is resolved, that Phase-1A is supplied, that EVIDENCE or TM is unblocked, that RT23-B-RES-01 is closed, or that an accepted retention artifact exists; every regex match is a negation or a 'stays' statement. Authority hygiene is CLEAN: zero decision ids appear as keys anywhere in the delta file; the single occurrence in the resolved value, $.dischargeStatus.CD-RT-5, is inherited verbatim from v8 and is the exact site the instrument guards. I VERIFIED THE ONE THING THIS FILE ACTUALLY DOES, BY COUNTERFACTUAL: with versioning-policy.v14.json removed from an isolated copy of the tree, check-product-dispositions-v2.py exits 1, 'product dispositions INVALID', on exactly one live conflict - versioning-policy.v8.json$.dischargeStatus.CD-RT-5; with the file present it exits 0. THE BLOCKER IS NOT ABOUT ANY OF THAT. It is one sentence, repeated 22 times in the keyLocator, that is FALSE at three positions and MATERIALLY false at one. 'It is NOT in this file' is asserted of knownLimitations, artifact and status, and all three ARE top-level keys of this file. At knownLimitations the two values differ: the file's own array has 6 entries about the delta, the resolved contract's has 17, and a reader who greps - which is the exact failure this corpus records FIVE times and which the keyLocator exists to prevent - silently exchanges seventeen contract caveats including 'Every support window is GUESSED and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED' for six statements about a delta file. The READ_THIS block enumerates the colliding names as 'status, reviewState ... author' and that enumeration omits knownLimitations, the only collision where the values differ. That is this lineage's own recurring defect one layer over: a repair performed narrowly and asserted broadly, in the one mitigation the artifact leans on hardest. The artifact's own success criterion, written in its own words, is a keyLocator 'that answers the exact question the failed greps were asking'; at knownLimitations it answers that question wrong. The remedy is two sentences and no re-measurement, and none of the verified work above is disturbed by it.

environmentAtMyVerdict.concurrencyHazardEncountered: The session scratchpad is SHARED and other lanes were actively writing to it during my review. A file I wrote as resolved.json was clobbered by a concurrent lane between two of my own reads, producing one incoherent intermediate result. I detected it because the top-level key set was impossible for the subject, discarded that run entirely, moved to a uniquely-named private subdirectory, and re-ran every measurement in a single process. EVERY NUMBER IN THIS ARTIFACT COMES FROM THE CLEAN RE-RUN. I record this because it is a fact about this review's conditions under freeze 7.2.1 item 4, and because it is a live hazard for any lane measuring in that directory.

howIResolvedTheDerivation.why: Freeze 7.3 and CMP-IR-01: a derivation must be RESOLVED, not read. The subject states that reading it instead of resolving it produced a wrong answer five times in this corpus, so I wrote my own resolver rather than trusting its description of itself.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.parse: Both the subject and versioning-policy.v8.json parsed with an object_pairs_hook that RAISES on any repeated name at any depth. Zero duplicates in either file. This closes B-VER12R-01's class at my end independently of the subject's claim to have done so.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.predecessorPin: derivation.predecessorSha256 = ea4b52b5a4d187ec35ad994d8ffcd888db287566c8fb53f3df17e5203d84ae2e equals the live sha256 of versioning-policy.v8.json. Verified, not assumed.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.comparator: I wrote my own strict-equality function rather than using the subject's description of one. It tests isinstance(x, bool) BEFORE isinstance(x, int) on both operands, so an integer respelling of a boolean is rejected rather than admitted - the hole v9's review measured at 15 of 139 boolean leaves. All six 'from' guards are str or int in this derivation, so no bool guard was exercised by the real data; I confirmed the rule is correctly STATED and that my resolver implements it, and I did not need it to resolve.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.pathHandling: Paths are arrays of tokens. I navigated by token type - JSON string as object key, JSON integer as array index - and never parsed pathDisplay, which the subject correctly declares non-normative. I confirmed pathDisplay agrees with path on all 8 operations anyway.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.guards: All six 'set' operations required the target to EXIST and its live value to be strictly equal to 'from'; all six passed. Both 'add' operations required the final key to be ABSENT from an existing parent object; both passed. Neither 'add' carries a 'from', which is correct for its kind.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.result: sha256(json.dumps(resolved, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')).encode('utf-8')) = 324845b22b3b1aed0dca9deb8fbc032048dc1399da967062c9103332f06aba41, canonical length 156172 bytes. This EQUALS the published $.resolvedValue.sha256.
howIResolvedTheDerivation.digestIsNotAByteClaim: I checked specifically for B-VER13R-01's lesson, because that is what killed the predecessor. The subject's digest is declared over a PARSED value under a named serialisation expression, and $.resolvedValue.whatThisDigestIsNOT states in terms that it is not a byte property of any file and that nothing claims any file is byte-identical to any serialisation. I searched the delta and the resolved value for a byte-identity claim about any file and found none. The v13 failure mode - a byte gate that compares newline-translated read_text() - CANNOT ARISE HERE, because there is no byte gate and no companion checker to host one. The declaration is honest about being one layer above the bytes and does not slide.

I built a 22-name vocabulary of apparatus keys directly from the eleven blockers' own 'against' fields and remedies, then walked the full key set of every lineage member and of the resolved value.
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: Apparatus keys present: versioning-policy.v9 = 5 (notClaimed, checkerDisposition, d9CitationRepair, retainedResiduals, recordedInputs); v10 = 9 (adds evidenceEnforcementRepair, checkerEnforcesEveryDeclaredEvidenceLeaf, evidenceLeafEnforcement, residualRestatements); v11 = 14 (adds enforcementClosureRepair, prosePaperSealScan, coverageCensus, partitionClosure, registryPurity); v12 = 17 (adds proseAuthorityRepair, repointRehearsals, predecessorDisposition); v13 = 20 (adds parseAuthorityRepair, predecessorAttributionRepair, byteVersusModelClosure, bytesEqualTheSerialisedReconstruction). versioning-policy.v14.json = ZERO of 22. Its resolved value = ZERO of 22. versioning-policy.v8.json = ZERO of 22.

'paper seal', 'paper-seal' and 'byte-identical' occur ONLY inside v14's verbatim quotations of the predecessors' blocker TITLES; 'coverage census', 'enforcement registry', 'partition' and 'companion checker' occur ONLY inside the sentence DISCLAIMING them; 'mutation' occurs only in v8's inherited schema-migration prose. And structurally so rather than by assertion: the apparatus is absent because v8 never had it and no operation adds it, which is the same structural guarantee that protects rules, custodyClasses, versionedIdentities, supportWindows, conformanceTests, migrators and the comparison fixtures and schemas.

It is a reading of the reviews, not an independent adjudication of them.' That concession is accurate and it is exactly the work it left for me, so I did it.

The other NINE name a checker AND artifact-side leaves - so the claim as loosely paraphrased ('no blocker touches the artifact') would be FALSE, at 9 of 11. centralClaimAdjudications.corroboration: Four of the five reviews say so themselves in a field the author did not quote. B-VER10R-01 doesNotAffect: 'Status, seal or discharge discipline, which are byte-identical to v9 and correct.' B-VER11R-01: '...byte-identical to v10 and correct; I could not move any of them.' B-VER12R-01: '...byte-identical to v11 and which I could not move.' B-VER13R-01 doesNotAffect names the duplicate-key closure, the reconstruction, the parse census, the parse-site scan, the partitions, the coverage census and the prose-authority partition - all apparatus, no contract.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: TRUE AS WRITTEN, and I confirm it independently rather than by relaying the author's reading. None of the eleven names rules, custodyClasses, versionedIdentities, supportWindows, conformanceTests, migrators, comparisonFixtures, comparisonSchema, decisionDependencies, principle, purpose or dischargeStatus. The distinction the sentence draws is real and load-bearing, not a rhetorical escape.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: 'Having no apparatus' is a repair rather than an evasion.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: REPAIR, and I want to be precise about why, because the opposite reading is available and the dispatch asked for it. A document that claims less can be under-specified. This one is not, because the apparatus it drops was never discharging a contract obligation - it was discharging a self-imposed one. v9 through v13 transcribed a reviewed 173 kB contract and then built machinery to prove the transcription faithful; the machinery is what failed, eleven times. A derivation does not transcribe, so the obligation the machinery served DOES NOT EXIST, and dropping the machinery removes a proof burden rather than a property. I verified the antecedent structurally rather than taking it on faith: the resolved value's 22 untouched predecessor keys are byte-equal to v8's, not re-typed, and notInTheOperationList is exactly those 22.
centralClaimAdjudications.andWhereItIsNotARepair: The omission is honest but it is not free, and the subject says so in the right direction: knownLimitations[0] concedes no retained checker validates this file and that freeze 7.2.2 grades a self-certifying artifact as weaker evidence than a retained instrument 'even when its numbers are right', and knownLimitations[5] concedes the file's own top-level structure is validated by nothing. I confirm both. What replaces the apparatus is not an instrument but a REPRODUCIBLE CONSTANT: the resolved digest, which any reviewer can recompute in ten lines and which I did recompute. That is a weaker guarantee than a retained checker and a stronger one than a banner, and the artifact places itself there accurately.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: check-product-dispositions-v2.py reports the predecessor's BLOCKED value as a live conflict, and this successor's mere existence demotes that live finding to a historical observation (the instrument's own residual R3).
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: Verified by counterfactual in an isolated full copy of the tree. WITH versioning-policy.v14.json present: EXIT 0, 'product dispositions OK', conflicting assertions in LIVE artifacts = 0, demoted to observations = 43 across 38 artifacts, and versioning-policy.v8.json is classified 'SUPERSEDED: superseded by versioning-policy.v14.json'. WITHOUT the file: EXIT 1, 'product dispositions INVALID', conflicting assertions in LIVE artifacts = 1, and the single failing finding is 'PD2-SCAN-CONFLICT versioning-policy.v8.json$.dischargeStatus.CD-RT-5: asserts CD-RT-5 PENDING (via blocked) while the binding product packet records CLOSED_POSITIVE'.
centralClaimAdjudications.r3Verbatim: The instrument prints, verbatim: 'R3  one substantive key makes a successor; repair QUALITY is not graded, so a near-stub successor demotes its predecessor.' The subject's residual [4] paraphrases this accurately and cites it as the instrument's residual, not as its own achievement.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: BOTH HALVES TRUE, and the second half is the sharpest fact about this artifact. It is recorded as observation O-05 below rather than as a blocker, because the subject DECLARED it in advance, unprompted, in writing, and published the resolved-value digest for the stated purpose of letting a reviewer 'check the repair instead of taking the demotion on trust' - which is exactly what I did. The residual belongs to the instrument. But a signer must not read the post-v14 exit 0 as evidence about v14.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: The named D9 version divergence is still OPEN and this successor does not close it.
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: CONFIRMED GENUINELY OPEN, not quietly closed. In the resolved value, $.decisionDependencies[4].source is still the string 'artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json' against D9 head v1.14. No operation names decisionDependencies; it is one of the 22 keys I verified byte-equal to the predecessor. The freeze's own section 3 VERSIONING row records the same divergence independently, folded per 7.7: 'Named version divergence, detected 2026-08-03 (not repairable in place). versioning-policy.v8 is the head and it is PASSED, but its decisionDependencies[4].source cites artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.6.json - eight versions behind the D9 head v1.14.'
centralClaimAdjudications.andTheAuthorsRefusalToCloseItIsCorrect: Closing it needs a v1.6-to-v1.14 re-measurement. The subject states it did not take that measurement and that republishing another lane's measurement as its own is the freeze 7.2.2 error. I agree, and I note the same discipline is applied to the RT23 figures: the subject cites 0 of 9 / 0 of 9 / 0 of 19 explicitly as the packet's record and states in capitals that it did not re-measure them. I did not re-measure them either, and I say so in whatIDidNotCheck.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: TRUE, and correctly refused. See O-03 for the one place the residual is scoped narrower than the divergence actually reaches.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: Authority hygiene - v14 cites CD-RT-5 and never constitutes it.
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: Zero decision ids appear as a KEY at any depth in versioning-policy.v14.json (regex CD-[A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]+ over every key at every depth). Exactly one appears in the resolved value, $.dischargeStatus.CD-RT-5, and it is present in versioning-policy.v8.json identically - inherited, not introduced, and it is the precise site check-product-dispositions-v2.py guards, so its presence is the mechanism rather than the hazard. Every element is faithful. See O-06 for one clause that is a condensation rather than the copy it is billed as.

blockers.notAgainst: The derivation, the resolution algorithm, the resolved value, the published digest, the leaf census, the operation accounting, the lineage account, the authority hygiene or the contract. I reproduced every one of those exactly and could not falsify any of them. No byte of the versioning contract is wrong, and the single substantive operation is correct.
blockers.title: The keyLocator asserts 'It is NOT in this file' of three keys that ARE top-level keys of this file, and at knownLimitations the two values differ - so the one mitigation built to make a grep safe returns a wrong answer about the contract at the one position where being wrong costs something.
blockers.theClaimUnderTest: $.keyLocator.knownLimitations, verbatim: 'INHERITED UNCHANGED from versioning-policy.v8.json. It is NOT in this file. Resolve the derivation to read it.' The same sentence is asserted of artifact and status. The block that directs readers here says the keyLocator 'lists every top-level key of the RESOLVED document and says, for each, whether this derivation changes it ... or whether it is inherited unchanged and therefore absent from this file. A grep against these bytes answers a different question than the one you are asking.' And whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theCostAndWhyItIsPaid names it as one of three mitigations: 'a keyLocator that answers the exact question the failed greps were asking'.
blockers.whatTheMechanismActuallyIs: The keyLocator is exact as a MAP FROM RESOLVED KEYS - 30 entries, 30 resolved top-level keys, no gap, no invention, every verb correct about inheritance and every operation index right. I verified all of that and it holds. What is false is the second sentence of the INHERITED template, which makes a claim about THIS FILE'S BYTES rather than about the resolved value. The delta file has 19 top-level keys and the resolved document has 30; the two sets INTERSECT AT SIX NAMES - artifact, author, knownLimitations, status, supersedes, version. For author, supersedes and version the keyLocator correctly says CHANGED and no falsehood is asserted. For artifact, status and knownLimitations it asserts 'It is NOT in this file', and all three are present.
blockers.measured: Of the three, artifact and status happen to carry values identical in both documents ('opensip.versioning-policy'; 'CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED'), so a misreading there is harmless and the falsehood is merely literal. knownLimitations is the material one: THE DELTA'S ARRAY HAS 6 ENTRIES AND THE RESOLVED CONTRACT'S HAS 17, and they share no element. A reader who greps knownLimitations in these bytes receives 'No retained checker validates this file', 'NAME COLLISION, OBSERVED AND DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED', 'The lineage account quotes each review's declared verdict string...', 'The claim that no blocking finding in the five is against the versioning contract rests on reading...', 'The resolved-value digest binds a canonical serialisation of a parsed value...' and 'This file's own top-level structure is not validated by anything' - six statements about a delta file - IN PLACE OF the contract's seventeen, which include 'Every support window is GUESSED and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED. VT-12's harness may be unbuildable by design.', 'The run-manifest migrator is NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE, so evidence bundles are USER-CUSTODY by V7 with no migrator', 'Migrators are specified, not written.', 'No production store/transaction implementation or atomicity evidence exists; candidate remains not applied' and 'The raw authority lineage is mechanically specified but not executed or independently accepted.'
blockers.whyThisIsBlockingAndNotAnObservation: Four reasons, and I weighed the opposite reading seriously before landing here. FIRST, THE DIRECTION OF THE ERROR READS AS VALIDATION. Seventeen contract caveats are exchanged for six delta caveats, and the seventeen are precisely the ones an implementer needs - guessed support windows, unwritten migrators, no atomicity evidence, an unexecuted authority lineage. A reader ends up with a MORE reassuring picture of the contract than the contract states. SECOND, THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE THE FILE EXISTS TO PREVENT, AT THE POSITION IT MISSED. The artifact states that reading a derivation instead of resolving it 'produced a wrong answer FIVE times in this corpus' and pays a declared cost to mitigate it; the mitigation misfires for exactly the reader who does not resolve. THIRD, THE ARTIFACT ALREADY TRIED TO CLOSE THIS CLASS AND CLOSED IT INCOMPLETELY. The READ_THIS block enumerates the colliding names - 'status, reviewState against the resolved document's reviewStatus, author' - and that list omits artifact and, decisively, knownLimitations, the ONE collision where the values differ. An enumeration that names the harmless collisions and misses the harmful one is the same shape as B-VER10R-01, B-VER11R-01 and B-VER12R-01: a scoped repair asserted unscoped, in a neighbourhood where every other claim is scrupulously scoped. FOURTH, THE ARTIFACT'S OWN SUCCESS CRITERION IS THE ONE IT FAILS. It claims a keyLocator 'that answers the exact question the failed greps were asking'. At knownLimitations, it answers that exact question wrong.
blockers.whyTheLineageStandardRequiresIt: I applied the standard this lineage's own reviewers applied to its predecessors, because applying a softer one to the sixth candidate would be the corpus grading by fatigue. B-VER11R-01 was BLOCKING on exactly this construction: 'Read as this closes the enumerated patterns in free prose it is TRUE ... Read as what it says - this closes the class in free prose - it is FALSE.' Here: read as 'the resolved value of this key is not in this file' it is TRUE; read as what it says, 'It is NOT in this file', it is FALSE at three of twenty-two positions and materially false at one.
blockers.andWhatIAmNotSaying: I am not saying the artifact is wrong about anything it measured, and I am not manufacturing a blocker to match a five-for-five pattern. I looked hard for the failures this lineage has produced before and did not find them: the digest is not a byte claim, the census is not self-referential, there is no registry sized from the artifact, no partition printed and uncompared, no repoint cost, no paper seal, no duplicate key, no fabricated authority, no overstatement, and no companion checker to be green about any of it. Every number this file publishes about itself, I recomputed, and every one was right. This blocker is one sentence used twenty-two times, wrong at three of them, and it happens to sit in load-bearing navigation.
remedy: In the keyLocator's INHERITED template, replace the unconditional 'It is NOT in this file.' with a statement that is true of every key it is applied to - e.g. 'Its RESOLVED VALUE is not in this file.' That single word change makes all 22 entries true and costs no re-measurement.

For the three colliding keys, say so explicitly and in the direction that stops the grep: for knownLimitations, 'CAUTION: this file has its own top-level knownLimitations (6 entries, about this delta). The resolved document's has 17 and is a different array. Resolve the derivation.' For artifact and status, note that the file's own value coincides and that the coincidence is not a guarantee.

Extend the READ_THIS_BEFORE_READING_ANY_OTHER_KEY enumeration from 'status, reviewState ... author' to the measured collision set - artifact, author, knownLimitations, status, supersedes, version - and state it as a measured count of six, the way every other boundary in this file is stated.
Consider stating the collision set as a derived fact rather than a hand-written list, since a hand-written enumeration of one's own key overlap is the thing that just went stale.
doesNotAffect: The resolved-value digest, which I reproduced exactly at 324845b22b3b1aed0dca9deb8fbc032048dc1399da967062c9103332f06aba41.
The keyLocator's completeness or its inheritance and operation-index verbs, all of which I verified at 30 of 30.
The leaf census, which I reproduced exactly in all ten categories.
The operation accounting or notInTheOperationList, which I reproduced exactly at 8/6/2 and 22 of 22.
The lineage account, whose ten digests, five verdicts, ten counts and eleven blocker titles I verified against live review bytes.
The single substantive operation, the authority hygiene, the residual declarations or the overstatement discipline, all of which are clean.
The central negative claim, which is true.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Six items are described as 'the five things'.
nonBlockingObservations.measured: $.whatThisFileDoesNotClaim[7], verbatim: 'It publishes no coverage census of the contract, no enforcement registry, no partition, no paper-seal scan, no repoint-cost estimate and no byte-identity claim. Those are the five things the five rejected successors were rejected for.' The enumeration has SIX members. The parallel sentence in the resolved value, whatV14DoesDifferently, lists SEVEN (adding 'no companion checker') and correctly attaches no number to them.
nonBlockingObservations.adjudication: A count stated against an adjacent enumeration and not recomputed. Harmless in substance - all six omissions are real and I verified each - but this corpus's own standard is that 'a figure you enumerate and do not recompute is exactly the figure a companion instrument will let you fabricate', and the arithmetic here is a six-item list. The likely intent is that FIVE successors were rejected; write the count of the list or drop it.

More to the point, the packet's own coordinatorAmendmentRecord names the cause: 'positionsRepaired: $.status, $.invariants[4], $.knownLimitations[0]', 'foundBy: the lane authoring v10-disposition.v2 and versioning-policy.v14, not by any instrument'.
